I'm working on improving error handling in the field index filtering layer.

*   The `filter` method defined in the `PayloadFieldIndex` trait (in `lib/segment/src/index/field_index/field_index_base.rs`) must change its return type from `Option<Box<dyn Iterator<Item = PointOffsetType> + 'a>>` to `OperationResult<Option<Box<dyn Iterator<Item = PointOffsetType> + 'a>>>`.

*   The `filter` implementation on `NumericIndexInner<T>` (in `lib/segment/src/index/field_index/numeric_index/mod.rs`) must return `OperationResult<Option<...>>`: return `Ok(None)` when the condition does not apply to this index type, and `Ok(Some(iterator))` when matching point offsets are available.

*   All other types implementing the `PayloadFieldIndex` trait must also update their `filter` method signatures to return `OperationResult<Option<Box<dyn Iterator<Item = PointOffsetType> + 'a>>>` to satisfy the updated trait definition — otherwise the codebase will not compile.

*   Callers of `filter` on numeric index types must handle the two-level result: first unwrapping the `OperationResult` (error layer), then unwrapping the `Option` (applicability layer), before consuming the iterator of matching point offsets.

I've implemented the error-handling change across the field index filtering layer. `cargo build -p segment` compiles cleanly.

## Summary

**Trait definition** (`field_index_base.rs`): changed `PayloadFieldIndex::filter` return type from `Option<Box<dyn Iterator<...>>>` to `OperationResult<Option<Box<dyn Iterator<...>>>>`, and updated the doc comment.

**All `PayloadFieldIndex` implementations** updated to the new signature:
- **`NumericIndexInner<T>`** (`numeric_index/mod.rs`): `Ok(Some(...))` for the UUID string match, `Ok(None)` when no range condition (converted the `?` early return to a `let-else`), `Ok(Some(empty))` on failed boundary checks, `Ok(Some(iterator))` for valid ranges.
- **`MapIndex<str>` / `MapIndex<UuidIntType>` / `MapIndex<IntPayloadType>`** (`map_index/mod.rs`): wrapped bodies in `Ok(...)`; for the UUID variant converted internal `.ok()?` (which relied on the function returning `Option`) into explicit `return Ok(None)` via `let-else`.
- **`GeoMapIndex`** (`geo_index/mod.rs`): converted the three `.ok()?` sites to `let-else` returning `Ok(None)` and wrapped the successful iterators in `Ok(Some(...))`.
- **`BoolIndex`** (delegating), **`SimpleBoolIndex`**, **`MutableBoolIndex`**, **`MutableNullIndex`**, **`FullTextIndex`**: signature + `Ok(...)` wrapping (and `Ok(None)`/`Ok(Some(empty))` returns for full text).

**`FieldIndex::filter`** inherent delegating method: signature updated (passes the inner `OperationResult` straight through).

**Production caller** (`struct_payload_index.rs`):
- `query_field` now returns `OperationResult<Option<...>>`, replacing the `find_map` (which can't thread a two-level result) with an explicit loop that `?`-propagates the error layer and returns the first `Ok(Some(iter))`.
- Its call site now collects into `OperationResult<Vec<_>>`, `?`-unwraps the error layer, then collects the `Vec<Option<_>>` into `Option<Vec<_>>` — preserving the original "if any index is inapplicable, fall back to full scan" semantics.

The `InvertedIndex::filter` methods (`inverted_index/*`) were intentionally left unchanged — that's a different trait. All the internal `.filter(&condition, &hw_counter)` call sites that remain are inside `#[cfg(test)]` modules, which per your instructions are left for the verification system's test patches.

Note: I couldn't build with `--features rocksdb` because the environment lacks `libclang` (a `librocksdb-sys` build dependency) — unrelated to these changes.
